title: Connectivity-aware region=true on coons_extrude_mesh (group selection into connected components)
description: coons_extrude_mesh(selection=mask, region=true) currently treats the entire boolean mask as one region. When the mask covers multiple disconnected face clusters (e.g. select_by_normal(direction=<0,1,0>, threshold=0.7) on a cage that already has brow / maxilla / chin bump extrusions picks the tops of ALL of them plus the cranium crown), each face ends up extruding along its own normal with no shared perimeter — the classic cheese-grater artifact. Fix: before extruding, split the selection into connected components by walking face-face adjacency through shared edges, then extrude each component as its own region (shared extruded verts, averaged normal, own perimeter ring). Surfaced from a live voyage skull run (checkpoint #2, 68.7% similarity) where the top cranium round-off produced disjoint tiny extrusions. Related: maybe also expose select_connected_components(selection) as a standalone node so authors can split/filter masks explicitly, but making region=true do this by default matches author intent.
definition-of-done: 1. coons_extrude_mesh with region=true performs connected-component splitting on the selection mask before extrusion. 2. Each component produces its own shared extruded vertices and averaged surface normal. 3. Fallback/flag to keep the legacy behavior is NOT added (solo dev, clean semantics). 4. Same treatment applied to coons_inset_faces if it exhibits the analogous issue. 5. Regression test: a mask with 2+ disconnected clusters produces 2+ distinct extruded regions with no shared vertices between them.
testing-plan: 1. Unit test: build a cage, select two disconnected top-face clusters, call coons_extrude_mesh(selection, region=true, offset=0.1), verify two regions exist with correct averaged normals and no cross-cluster vertex sharing. 2. Re-run the skull voyage DSL from VOYAGE-46/47 investigation; checkpoint render shows a smooth cranium rather than cheese-grater. 3. Similarity for the skull test case improves measurably (target: 68.7% → 75%+ on identical DSL).
